suite: Cornered by a serial killer who hurt my ...
user_input: When he lunges, I grab his wrist with both hands and slam him into the doorway before he can cut me. I keep my feet planted and knock the weapon out of his hand.
contexts: I’m backed into the kitchen corner of my childhood home, the tile cold and slick under my bare feet, and he’s standing in the doorway with that same blank stare, his weapon hanging loose in his hand like he already knows he doesn’t have to rush. contexts: I’m trapped in a burned-out church, the air thick with smoke and the bitter stink of sulfur, and this thing in front of me keeps smiling with a mouth full of black, broken teeth even after I hack pieces off of it. Every time my blade sinks into its flesh, I hear wet tearing and bone cracking, but the severed limbs twitch on the stone floor and pull themselves back, stitching together with strings of red muscle while it crawls toward me faster than it should be able to. My arms feel heavy and numb, my chest burns, and I can hear my own panicked breathing echoing with its low, laughing growl as its hollow eyes lock on mine. I realize all at once that hurting it means nothing, that I have to destroy every part of it completely, and when I look down the floor is already writhing with pieces of it grabbing at my ankles as the main body lunges for my throat.

People rush past me shoulder to shoulder, their voices sharp and loud, and every time I try to ask for help, only broken, useless sounds come out of my mouth while they stare at me with irritation or blank indifference. My chest feels tight and cold, my shoes slip on the wet pavement, and I realize I have no phone, no map, no idea where I am as the streets keep twisting back into themselves no matter which way I run. Then I turn a corner into a dead-end alley and hear fast footsteps closing in behind me, and when I open my mouth to scream, I still can’t make a single word come out.

suite: Failing a test in front of a mocking aud...
user_input: I stand up before the loudspeaker can humiliate me and turn to face everyone. I tell them to stop laughing, and my voice comes out steady enough that the room finally goes quiet.
contexts: I’m sitting alone at a tiny desk in the middle of a huge auditorium, the test paper trembling in my sweaty hands, and when I look down the words keep sliding off the page like ink in water so I can’t read a single question. The room is unnaturally bright, hot against my skin, and I can hear hundreds of people breathing and whispering behind me until the whispers turn into snickering, then full laughter, sharp and echoing off the walls. Every time I try to write, my pencil snaps or my hand goes numb, and when I look up I see rows of faces staring at me—teachers, strangers, people I know—all smiling like they’ve been waiting for me to fail. Then my name booms over a loudspeaker, the clock starts pounding louder than a heartbeat, and I realize I’m supposed to stand up and read my blank answers out loud as the audience rises to its feet, pointing at me and laughing.

contexts: I’m running down a dark street that seems to stretch forever, my chest burning, and then I see them lying on the cold pavement under a flickering yellow streetlight, twisted in a way that makes my stomach drop. Their clothes are soaked and shining black-red, and when I fall to my knees beside them, my hands slip on something warm and sticky while a low ringing fills my ears and drowns out my own voice calling their name. Their eyes flutter open just enough to look at me, terrified, and their mouth moves like they’re trying to say something, but all that comes out is a wet, choking sound that I can feel in my bones. I try to press my hands over the wound, but the blood keeps pushing through my fingers, hotter and faster, and I realize they’re going still while I’m screaming for help into the empty, silent street.
